As Apple (AAPL) Valuation Declined, Holder Berkshire Hathaway Raised Its Position; As Vodafone Group Adr (VOD) Stock Value Declined, Shareholder Hanson & Doremus Investment Management Has Trimmed by $341,062 Its Stake 
April 10, 2018 - By Michael Collier 
Warren Buffett increased its stake in Apple Inc (AAPL) by 23.3% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Berkshire Hathaway Inc bought 31.24M shares as the company’s stock declined 3.81% with the market. The hedge fund run by Warren Buffett held 165.33 million shares of the computer manufacturing company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $27.98 billion, up from 134.09 million at the end of the previous reported quarter. Berkshire Hathaway Inc who had been investing in Apple Inc for a number of months, seems to be bullish on the $879.88B market cap company. The stock increased 1.98% or $3.36   $173.41. About 24.80 million shares traded. Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) has risen 19.49%   uptrending. It has outperformed by 7.94% the S&P500. 
Hanson & Doremus Investment Management decreased its stake in Vodafone Group Adr (VOD) by 12.29% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Hanson & Doremus Investment Management sold 11,002 shares as the company’s stock declined 13.40% with the market. The institutional investor held 78,508 shares of the telecommunications equipment company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $2.50M, down from 89,510 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Hanson & Doremus Investment Management who had been investing in Vodafone Group Adr for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $76.30B market cap company. The stock increased 1.73% or $0.5   $29.45. About 2.39M shares traded. Vodafone Group Plc (NASDAQ:VOD) has risen 2.53%   uptrending. It has underperformed by 9.02% the S&P500.
